main_text.p: scripta volo adversus Virum alium erudi-tum qui nihil plane novi dicit, Coteler. Epist. ad Magnef. pag. 449nec quic-quam notatu dignum observat; nisi quod se commendabilem reddere voluit: Virum doctissimum Ioannem Dallæum, iniquè deprimedo,& Dionysium Petavium suprà illum adulatoriè nimis extollendo; nem-pe Petavij vestigia premens, Valentinia-norum sigen, de nudo silentio interpreta-tur, ideóque tanti Viri autoritate, à quo sua accepit, infrunitam de Sige sententiam se posse tueri gaudet. Verùm pro-ptereà Dallæum traducere non debebat; nec quicquam causæ erat cur illi injurio-sè insultaret, eúmque elato supercilio de-spiceret; Nam Vir iste in hisce studijs, Dallæo longè est inferior nec in scriptis Patrum æquè ac ille versatus; cum Dal-læus in Antiquitatis monumentis exerci-tatissimus illa penitùs combiberit, & in succum quodammodò verterit.

XV. Explosis Vindiciarum auctoris rationi-bus, quibus probare nitebatur, suorum Æonum primas Syzygias accepisse Valentinianos à Gnosticis Valentino vetu-stioribus, expendendæ superfunt quas ad Dallæi argumenta adfert exceptiones; primum cui occurrit argumentum ex va-riis Tertulliani locis depromptum est: Tertullianus siquidem de Præscript. cap.

page.notes: The first word of the page continues a sentence from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". A small mark (possibly a printer's asterisk) stands before "Verùm"; it is left out. The final "cap." is set in bold in print; bold is not marked here. The hyphen in "erudi-" and similar line-end breaks is a printed hyphen and is kept. The margin note is set in italic and runs over four lines. No catchword or signature is printed on the page.
